children: ability to clarify how it will fund its AI infrastructure expansion will be key to improving investor sentiment ahead of its financial analyst meeting.

"The key to unlocking that value is giving investors a clearer picture of the remaining funding needs and a path to realizing the upside in OCI without putting further pressure on the balance sheet," analysts at Evercore said.
Oracle needs $50B to $60B in additional funding before free cash flow turns positive in fiscal 2029, Evercore estimates, highlighting concerns over capital spending and commitments tied to OpenAI

Oracle has forecast capital expenditure of $90B to $95B for fiscal 2027. Evercore said investors will look for more details on customer funding, alternative financing, and potential delays at data center projects.

Clarity on the quality of Oracle's remaining performance obligations, or contracted revenue yet to be recognized, particularly excluding OpenAI, as well as the growth outlook for its software business.

Evercore said Oracle's software and non-AI cloud businesses alone are worth about $197 per share on a debt-adjusted basis, based on its sum-of-the-parts analysis. It estimated the company's AI cloud infrastructure business is being assigned a negative value by the market, reflecting funding and execution risks.
Evercore kept its $245 price target, saying greater clarity on funding needs and data center delivery timelines could help Oracle shares recover.

title: Oracle's AI funding needs investor confidence, says Evercore
